newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures surge on higher CBOT, weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures surge on higher CBOT, weak yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended sharply higher on Tuesday as price gains on the Chicago corn market on Monday and the yen's slightly weaker sentiment against the dollar triggered active buying, traders said.
All contracts rose by the daily 400 yen limit by the close, and benchmark September 1998 was up 400 yen at 15,570 yen per tonne. Estimated volume was 81,169 lots.
Buying orders by local investors emerged from the opening, pushing all contracts up, traders said.
"Buying was accelerated by early afternoon. Price advances of CBOT overnight corn trading also encouraged investors," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system stood at $2.62-1/2 per bushel at 0745 GMT, against $2.60-3/4 at Monday's close.
Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.80 per bushel at 0745 GMT, against $7.85-1/2 at Monday's close.
